1: Why: 12 of v3's 18 approach violations (r3) were slow vertical legs shorter than 50 mm; one tool fixes all of that kind at once. Accepted +6.8 s, because legal comes before fast.
2: Why: 4 of the remaining 6 r3 hits were the guide's sideways slide into its closed side pocket. A vertical through-notch allows a grip from above (DFA: top-down handling). CAD + program together, because neither half works alone.
3: Why: 5 of 8 violations were the forearm (link 3) hitting planks 4/5 in the jig while it reached for the guide on base B. Moving the jig 60 mm away from that reach removes the cause instead of re-routing around it.
4: Why: r4 flagged the PTP lift-out starting only 50 mm above the frame grip. Both ends have the same tool orientation, so a straight Line rises vertically and is legal.
5: Why: the carried plank1 swept through the top of the already placed plank2 (r1). Measured it first (L07): needed more transit height, not a new route.
6: Why: the exit after the frame release was a slow sideways dogleg (~18 s at 20 mm/s, and an r3 hit). Leaving straight up the way it came in removes both.
7: Why: the last violation was a zero-depth contact of the plank ends on the base B pocket floor. A 2 mm relief under the plank ends should remove it. Rejected: it also removed the floor under 4 interface pieces (r6).
8: Why: iter 07's idea was right but the cut was too wide. Cut only the plank-end footprints minus the interface-piece footprints. First legal design.
9: Why: biggest phase = planks (127 s). The push after each release (close, push 20 mm, open) moved nothing: the release pose was already home (r8 still passes). Remove a whole handling step x6.
10: Why: the place descent was slow for 75 mm but the rule needs only the last 50 mm slow; 25 mm at 20 mm/s -> at 100 mm/s saves ~1 s per plank.
11: Why: guide phase (62 s) was long 100 mm/s Lines; a PTP over the same distance is faster (joint speed). Outbound transfer first.
12: Why: same evidence and change as iter 11, for the return transfer (~22 s of Lines).
13: Why: every plank pick/place went through a transit at TCP z 391 although the rules only need ~100 mm clearance; lower transits shorten 24 fast Lines.
14: Why: the frame-1 approach was 11.5 s of Lines and small PTPs via a detour; one PTP + one Line covers it.
15: Why: the retreat after the frame release was 3 Lines + a PTP (5.7 s); Line up + one PTP is shorter.
16: Why: still biggest phase planks; the slow lift after each plank grip was 60 mm where 50.5 mm is enough (same logic as iter 10, on the pick side).
17: Why: same 75 -> 50.5 mm slow-leg cut for the frame release.
18: Why: after releasing the guide the arm climbed to z 461, a height left over from v3's route; climb only as high as the next PTP needs.
19: Why: the longest PTP was J6-bound (232 deg); unwrapping J6 by +360 deg keeps the same pose with a shorter turn (lowering a PTP was tried first in screens and dropped, L19).
20: Why: the guide return grip turned J6 the long way from plank4; grip at J6 +180 and lift higher so the opposite flip clears plank6.
21: Why: a 244 mm Line dropped the guide straight down only because the PTP end had to stay 100 mm from a plank release point; move that PTP end sideways instead of up.
22: Why: plank transits sat at +117.5 mm because they were inside the plank's thin (5 mm) xy box; a 10 mm side offset leaves the box and lets them drop to +102 mm (24 Lines shorter).
23: Why: same side-offset idea for the guide-grip transits over base A (long 240 mm vertical Lines).
24: Why: start/end of the cycle cost 4 s of wrist-branch (J5) swings; put home on the joint path between the last lift and the first approach.
25: Why: the guide's trip to base A and back (~46 s) only serves as a placing aid; frame 1 already holds the planks upright alone, and no rule needs the trip. Lesson L25: question whether a phase is needed before tuning it.
26: Why: with the guide trip gone, the gap between plank jig and base A was free; moving the jig closer shortens 12 pick/place PTPs (got less than expected: those PTPs were J6-bound).
27: Why: five PTPs were J6-bound because planks 4-6 sit 80 deg turned in the frame vs the jig; present them pre-rotated (DFA: present parts in assembly orientation) and place them as a group.
28: Why: the end of the cycle was set by a 228 deg J5 swing; a PTP flip onto the other wrist branch (a Line could not, L24) shortens the return home.
29: Why: the 320 mm diagonal Line to the frame-foot grip was the longest single move left; end the PTP further down it.
30: Why: the lift after the frame grip climbed higher than r4 needs before the flip PTP; stop it lower (small, -0.5 s).
